### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `74ca2150e34cde2e14efe2292777e75dad7a050c` — the merge of head `57b8e00f539ad37037e24f398db50042e80a74cf` into base `84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 74ca2150e34cde2e14efe2292777e75dad7a050c && git checkout 74ca2150e34cde2e14efe2292777e75dad7a050c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998 57b8e00f539ad37037e24f398db50042e80a74cf && git checkout -B drift-repro 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998 && git merge --no-ff 57b8e00f539ad37037e24f398db50042e80a74cf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 84177cf21f5b3f06efb04711a2de3ea183ac1998` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (lane review, `TIER_DEFAULT`) · #32396 · head `4831a9b9` · 2026-11-11T16:11Z

| Item | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. First line `Fixes #32396`. 7 files, +907/−93: `metadata-protocol` (`protocol-history-and-publish.ts`, `protocol.ts`), a new 9-pin test, two test adjustments, the gate-written `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` row, and a patch changeset. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Not governed, 1000 lines ≤ 3000. No contract face, so no contract review is owed. |
| Premise, reproduced in-repo | The card's eleven drafts, refused at item 9 by the real `lint-autonumber-formats`, on an engine whose driver declares `transactionsUnsupported` (the remote Turso transport shape). Before the fix, items 1–8 stayed active while the answer said refused, `publishedCount: 0`; the store pin was red at `cd9f8961`. Cause: atomicity was chosen by `typeof engine.transaction === 'function'`, but the engine degrades to no rollback (ADR-0119 D1). |
| Fix | Only where `engineCanRollBack(engine)` is false: Phase 0 judges every draft before any write (`judgeOnly`); a Phase-1 failure undoes every landed promotion (created rows removed, edited rows restored, consumed drafts put back byte-identical, each through the registry view); an undo that fails is named in `failed[]`, `console.error` and the audit note. Runtimes that can roll back are unchanged. |
| Tests | 61 publish/draft/batch files of metadata-protocol: 1542 passed. 11 objectql publish files: 169 passed. Ablation of `engineCanRollBack`: 5 red, 4 green. Restore verified. |
| Deviations accepted | Single-file runs and the ablation ran outside the verify lock (a sibling held it for more than 30 min); the rest of the suites are left to CI Test Core. The ledger row was written by its own gate. |
| Out of scope | (b) A refused publish still runs the visibility flip → filed #32455. The card's Secondary item (`verify_build` / `create_metadata` do not surface the refusal before publish) → split to #32456, so `Fixes #32396` here closes only the main defect. The ADR-0067 D2 caveat line ("atomicity is a SQL-driver guarantee") no longer matches the remote Turso production transport. That is a Tier H ADR edit, so it goes to the maintainer in the seat's clock-out brief. |

Landing: on all-green checks, `check-expected-skips` + `check-governed-merges` + K, then `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
